title: MaxK-GNN: Extremely Fast GPU Kernel Design for Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Training
problem: GPUs experience workload imbalance and memory access irregularities when training Graph Neural Networks, leading to hardware underutilization. Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) operations generate excessive memory traffic that limits performance.
motivation: GPUs are the mainstream platform for deep neural network training, but their inefficiency on GNNs significantly limits training performance and scalability.
method: MaxK-GNN designs specialized GPU programs (kernels) that tackle the two main performance problems in GNN training: uneven work distribution and unpredictable memory access. It automatically balances the workload across GPU processing units and restructures how data is fetched from memory to make access patterns regular and predictable. This matters because GNN training involves Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM)—computing with matrices that mix mostly-zero sparse data with full matrices—which normally generates unpredictable memory traffic that slows everything down.
key_novelty: GPU kernels specially designed to handle the workload imbalance and unpredictable memory access patterns of sparse-dense matrix operations in GNN training.
contributions: Specialized GPU kernel design for accelerated GNN training
Addresses workload imbalance challenges in sparse GNN computations
Reduces memory traffic overhead in sparse-dense matrix multiplication
Outperforms existing frameworks including PyG, DGL, and GNNAdvisor

metrics.other: performance improvements claimed but specific metrics not provided
